title: IELTS Academic Test - Practice 1
description: A complete IELTS Academic practice test covering all four modules: Listening, Reading, Writing, and Speaking.

sections.title: Listening Module
sections.instructions: You will hear a number of different recordings and you will have to answer questions on what you hear. There will be time for you to read the instructions and questions, and you will have a chance to check your work. The recordings will be played once only. The test is in four sections. Write your answers on the question paper as you listen. At the end of the test, you will have 10 minutes to transfer your answers to an answer sheet.

questions.questionText: Which floor is the apartment on?

sections.title: Reading Module
sections.instructions: You should spend about 60 minutes on this section. There are three reading passages with a total of 40 questions. Answer all the questions. Write your answers on the answer sheet.

questions.questionText: According to the passage, what was the main cause of urban migration in the 19th century?
questions.passage: The Industrial Revolution of the late 18th and early 19th centuries had a profound effect on the social structure of Britain. As new factories and mills sprang up across the country, people flocked from rural areas to urban centers in search of work. This mass migration created huge, overcrowded cities with poor living conditions for many workers. The wealthy industrialists built grand houses away from the smoke and dirt of the factories, while workers often lived in cramped, unsanitary housing close to their places of employment.
options: Industrialization and availability of factory jobs
Higher wages in teaching and administrative roles
questions.correctAnswer: Industrialization and availability of factory jobs

sections.title: Writing Module
sections.instructions: You should spend about 60 minutes on this task. The Writing module consists of two tasks. Complete both tasks.

questions.questionText: The chart below shows the percentage of households with access to the internet in three different countries between 2000 and 2020. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

Task Achievement: Fully satisfies all requirements of the task
Clearly presents a fully developed response
Presents, highlights and illustrates key features clearly and appropriately
Lexical Resource: Uses a wide range of vocabulary fluently and flexibly
Makes only rare minor errors in word choice
Grammatical Range: Uses a wide range of structures

questions.sampleAnswer:
The line graph illustrates the percentage of households with internet access in three countries (Country A, Country B, and Country C) over a 20-year period from 2000 to 2020.

In 2000, Country A had the highest proportion of households connected to the internet at 30%, followed by Country B with 20%, while Country C lagged significantly behind at just 5%. Over the next decade, all three countries experienced steady growth in internet penetration, with Country A maintaining its lead, reaching 60% by 2010, compared to 45% in Country B and 30% in Country C.

The period from 2010 to 2020 saw dramatic changes in the relative positions. Country C demonstrated remarkable growth, overtaking both other countries with an impressive rise to 90% household internet access by 2020. Country B also showed substantial progress, reaching 80% by the end of the period. Surprisingly, Country A, despite being the early leader, showed the slowest growth rate in the second decade, ending at 75% in 2020, thus falling behind both other nations.

Overall, while Country A dominated internet access in the early years, Country C demonstrated the most dramatic improvement over the 20-year period, transforming from the lowest to the highest rate of household internet connectivity.

sections.title: Speaking Module
sections.instructions: The Speaking module consists of a face-to-face interview with a certified examiner. It lasts between 11 and 14 minutes and is divided into three parts.

speakingPrompts: Could you tell me your full name, please?
Can I see your identification, please?
Now I'd like to ask you some questions about yourself.
Let's talk about your home town or village. What's it like?
What do you like most about living there?
Would you like to live somewhere else in the future?

Lexical Resource: Uses vocabulary with full flexibility and precision

Makes only very occasional errors or inappropriacies
Pronunciation: Uses a full range of pronunciation features with precision and subtlety
Sustains flexible use of features throughout
